question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

He was able to do _____ (tedious) jobs and hence decide to be in the airline service, which demanded 12 long hours of service.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. delightful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tedious" means boring, dull and tiresome (especially because it is long or monotonous). Its antonym is "delightful", meaning highly pleasing and enjoyable. (उबाऊ का विलोम — आनंददायक)

◦ Example: The lecture was tedious, but the film afterwards was delightful.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "irksome" (annoying/tiresome) is a synonym of tedious.

• Option 3 "riotous" (wild/unruly) and Option 4 "timid" (shy) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tedious: boring, dull, monotonous, tiresome, wearisome.

• Antonyms: delightful, interesting, exciting, engaging, enjoyable.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment without changing its meaning in the given sentence.

Family planning programs play a crucial role in promoting reproductive health and empowering individuals to make informed choices, contributing to sustainable population growth and a healthier society.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. promoting a viable population increase.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Contributing to sustainable population growth" means helping bring about a balanced, manageable and viable increase in population. "Promoting a viable population increase" conveys the same positive, sustainable sense. (टिकाऊ जनसंख्या वृद्धि को बढ़ावा देना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "discouraging ... upsing" is meaningless/negative.

• Option 3 "sustainable population explosion" is contradictory (an "explosion" is not sustainable).

• Option 4 "unbalanced population growth" reverses the intended positive meaning.

NOTE

• "Sustainable" = able to be maintained at a steady level without harming the future. "Viable" = capable of working successfully; both suggest a balanced, healthy outcome.

question:
Based on the situation in the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment.

Having known to the facts, the manager disregarded the arguments of the customer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Turned a deaf ear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to turn a deaf ear" means to ignore or refuse to listen to something. It fits "disregarded the arguments of the customer". (अनसुना करना / ध्यान न देना)

◦ Example: The officer turned a deaf ear to their complaints.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "bite the bullet" (to face a difficulty bravely), Option 3 "turned out" (resulted/happened) and Option 4 "turned against" (became hostile) do not mean to ignore.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of ignoring: "turn a blind eye" (pretend not to notice), "fall on deaf ears" (be ignored), "give someone the cold shoulder".

question: Select the sentence that contains a spelling error.
option_1: They had been disgrunteled with the company due to various reasons.
option_2: Despite his formidable appearance, he possesses a kind heart.
option_3: We saw a pride of lions nonchalantly roaming in the forest.
option_4: He has made significant improvement in the last few weeks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They had been disgrunteled with the company due to various reasons.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "disgrunteled" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "disgruntled", meaning angry or dissatisfied. (असंतुष्ट / नाराज़)

◦ Correct: They had been disgruntled with the company due to various reasons.

• Spelling key: DIS + GRUNT + LED — there is no extra "e" before "led".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are correctly spelt — "formidable", "possesses", "nonchalantly" and "significant" are all spelt properly.

NOTE

• Related word: "gruntled" is rarely used; "disgruntled" (dissatisfied) is the common form. Synonyms: displeased, discontented, resentful.

question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment that has a grammatical error.

I left my / coat in the / hospital when I / had visit Alex.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. had visit Alex.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Had visit" is grammatically wrong. The correct form for a completed past action would be the simple past "visited" or "went to visit". A neat correction is "went to visit Alex".

◦ Correct: I left my coat in the hospital when I went to visit Alex.

• After "had", we need the past participle "visited" (had visited), but the context of the sentence works best as "went to visit".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "I left my", "coat in the" and "hospital when I" are all correct.

NOTE

• Verb forms: visit – visited – visited. After the auxiliary "had", use the past participle (had visited); "had visit" is never correct.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Vigorous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Energetic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vigorous" means strong, active and full of energy. Its closest synonym is "energetic". (जोरदार / ऊर्जावान)

◦ Example: He took a vigorous/energetic walk every morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Academic" (relating to study), Option 3 "Guarded" (cautious) and Option 4 "Furious" (very angry) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vigorous: energetic, dynamic, robust, forceful, spirited.

• Antonyms: weak, feeble, lethargic, sluggish.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Contrary
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Similar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Contrary" means opposite in nature, direction or meaning. Its antonym is "similar", meaning alike or resembling. (विपरीत का विलोम — समान)

◦ Example: Their opinions were contrary to each other, though their backgrounds were similar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Reverse" is a synonym of contrary.

• Option 1 "Transformational" (causing change) and Option 4 "Forward" (ahead) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of contrary: opposite, opposing, conflicting, contradictory, reverse.

• Antonyms: similar, alike, corresponding, same, agreeing.

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

They needed a __________ answer for every question.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. precise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There is no comparison in the sentence, so the positive degree "precise" (exact and accurate) is correct. "They needed a precise answer for every question." (सटीक / यथार्थ)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more precise" (comparative) and Option 3 "most precise" (superlative) are not needed as there is no comparison.

• Option 4 "preciser" is not the correct comparative form (it is "more precise").

NOTE

• Degrees of "precise": precise – more precise – most precise (long adjectives take "more/most", not "-er/-est"). Use the positive degree when simply describing without comparison.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The CEO came up with a groundbreaking strategy to __________ new markets and capitalise on emerging trends.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. break into.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "break into" (in a business sense) means to successfully enter a new market or field. So the CEO's strategy was to "break into new markets". (नए बाज़ारों में प्रवेश करना)

◦ Example: The company hopes to break into the Asian market next year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "break off" (to end suddenly), Option 2 "break out" (to escape / start suddenly) and Option 3 "break down" (to stop working / collapse) do not fit.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "break": break into (enter a market / enter by force), break down (fail/collapse), break out (escape/erupt), break off (discontinue), break up (separate).

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word.

She has a magnificient personality.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Magnificent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Magnificent", meaning extremely beautiful, impressive or grand. (शानदार / भव्य)

◦ Example: The palace had a magnificent garden.

• Spelling key: MAG + NI + FI + CENT — note "magni-" (great) and the ending "-cent" (no extra "i" before "ent").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Megnificent", 2 "Magnificient" and 4 "Megnificint" are all misspellings (wrong vowels/extra "i").

NOTE

• Related words: magnificent (adjective), magnificence (noun), magnificently (adverb). The root "magni-" means "great" (as in magnify, magnitude, magnanimous).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

The walls of the marriage hall were covered by beautiful purple curtains.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. covered with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When something is spread over a surface, we use "covered with". So "the walls ... were covered with beautiful purple curtains". ("Covered by" is used more for the agent/doer in the passive, but "covered with" is correct for the covering material.) (से ढका हुआ)

◦ Correct: The walls of the marriage hall were covered with beautiful purple curtains.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "covered upon / of / on" are not the correct prepositions for describing a covering material.

NOTE

• "Covered with" (a material/substance): covered with snow, covered with dust, covered with curtains. "Covered by" often indicates the agent (covered by insurance / covered by the roof).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Haste
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Delay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Haste" means excessive speed or urgency in doing something; hurry. Its antonym is "delay", meaning a slowing down or postponement. (जल्दबाजी का विलोम — देरी)

◦ Example: In his haste, he forgot his keys; a little delay would have saved him the trouble.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Speed" and Option 4 "Quick" are close to synonyms of haste.

• Option 3 "Twist" (to turn) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of haste: hurry, rush, speed, urgency.

• Antonyms: delay, slowness, leisure, deliberation. Proverb: "Haste makes waste"; "More haste, less speed".

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: The teacher from a South explained the theory in the detailed manner.
option_2: A teacher from South explained the theory in the detailed manners.
option_3: The teacher from the South explained the theory in a detailed manner.
option_4: The teacher from an South explained a theory in the detailed manner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The teacher from the South explained the theory in a detailed manner.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sentence uses "the South" (a specific region takes "the"), "the theory" (a specific theory) and "in a detailed manner" (the indefinite article "a" with the singular "manner").

◦ Correct: The teacher from the South explained the theory in a detailed manner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "from a South" is wrong (directions/regions take "the").

• Option 2 "detailed manners" (plural) is wrong; "manner" should be singular here.

• Option 4 "an South" is wrong ("South" begins with a consonant sound, so "the", not "an").

NOTE

• Use "the" with directions/regions used as nouns (the South, the North, the East). Use "a/an" by sound: "in a detailed manner", "an honest man".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

If 2023 was ___ year consumers helped stave off a recession with an unexpected surge in spending, many economists __________ 2024 will be the time shoppers finally tighten their belts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the, predict.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs the definite article "the" because "year" is specified by the following clause ("... consumers helped stave off a recession"). The second blank needs a verb that fits "economists ___ 2024 will be ...": "predict" (to forecast). (निश्चित वर्ष के लिए 'the'; भविष्यवाणी करना = predict)

◦ Correct: If 2023 was the year consumers helped stave off a recession ..., many economists predict 2024 will be the time ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "a/an year" is less precise for a specified year; "see/wanted" do not fit the forecasting sense as well as "predict".

NOTE

• Use "the" when a noun is made specific by a defining clause ("the year that ..."). "Predict" = to say what will happen in the future; economists "predict" trends.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Playing 'hide-n-seek' is the one of the fond memories of my childhood.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fondest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of the + superlative + plural noun" requires the superlative degree — "one of the fondest memories". The superlative of "fond" is "fondest".

◦ Correct: Playing 'hide-n-seek' is one of the fondest memories of my childhood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "most fondest" is a double superlative (both "most" and "-est") — wrong.

• Options 2 "fonder" and 3 "more fonder" are comparative forms (and "more fonder" is a double comparative).

NOTE

• Pattern: "one of the + superlative + plural noun" — one of the best players, one of the finest books, one of the fondest memories.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Pamper' from the given sentence.

I always feel that nuclear families always mollycoddle their kids without directing them to the correct path or denying their unrealistic demands.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mollycoddle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pamper" means to treat someone with excessive care and indulgence; to spoil/over-protect. Its synonym in the sentence is "mollycoddle" (to be overprotective and indulgent). (लाड़-प्यार करना / अत्यधिक दुलारना)

◦ Example: Grandparents often pamper/mollycoddle their grandchildren.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Path", 2 "Demands" and 3 "Nuclear" are other words from the sentence but do not mean "pamper".

NOTE

• Synonyms of pamper: mollycoddle, indulge, spoil, cosset, coddle.

• Antonyms: neglect, ignore, deprive.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The old man shared his __________ wisdom with the young generation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sagacious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sagacious" means wise, shrewd and showing good judgement. It fits "wisdom" — the old man's sagacious (wise) wisdom. (बुद्धिमान / विवेकशील)

◦ Example: The sagacious old teacher guided many students to success.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "trivial" (unimportant), Option 3 "ephemeral" (short-lived) and Option 4 "frivolous" (not serious) all carry a negative/unfitting sense with "wisdom".

NOTE

• Synonyms of sagacious: wise, shrewd, astute, prudent, judicious, discerning.

• Antonyms: foolish, unwise, imprudent.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Clear as mud
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Very difficult to understand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "clear as mud" is used ironically to mean that something is not clear at all — very confusing or difficult to understand. (बिल्कुल अस्पष्ट / समझ से परे)

◦ Example: His explanation of the theory was as clear as mud — nobody understood it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 take the phrase literally (mud, easy, clean) and miss the ironic meaning of being confusing.

NOTE

• "Clear as mud" is an example of irony — saying the opposite of what is meant. Similar ironic idioms: "as clear as day" (its opposite — very clear).

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The children were excited to ride the carusel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Carousel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Carousel", meaning a merry-go-round (a revolving amusement ride with model horses/seats). (झूला / मेरी-गो-राउंड)

◦ Example: The kids enjoyed a ride on the carousel at the fair.

• Spelling key: CAR + OU + SEL — one "r", one "l".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Carousell", 3 "Carrousel" and 4 "Karusel" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• A "carousel" also refers to the rotating conveyor belt at airports where luggage is collected (baggage carousel).

question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

Yash is not better than Harsh.
option_2: Yash is as good as Harsh.
option_3: Yash and Harsh both are good.
option_4: Yash is not good than Harsh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Yash is as good as Harsh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yash is not better than Harsh" (comparative) means Yash is at most equal to Harsh, i.e. the two are equally good. In the positive degree, this is expressed as "as good as".

◦ Correct: Yash is as good as Harsh.

• Rule: "A is not better than B" (comparative) = "A is as good as B" (positive degree).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "best than" wrongly mixes superlative with "than".

• Option 4 "not good than" is grammatically wrong ("good" cannot take "than").

NOTE

• Interchange of degrees: Comparative "not + comparative + than" → Positive "as + positive + as". E.g., "He is not taller than me" = "He is as tall as me".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We should remember that all religions (1)_______ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_______. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_______ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_______ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_______ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. preach.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Preach" means to advocate, teach or urge (a way of life or belief). Religions "preach good conduct in life" — they teach and promote good behaviour. (उपदेश देना / प्रचार करना)

◦ Correct: We should remember that all religions preach good conduct in life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "abandon" (to give up), Option 3 "refrain" (to hold back) and Option 4 "depart" (to leave) contradict the positive idea of teaching good conduct.

NOTE

• "Preach" = to deliver a religious/moral message or advocate strongly. Collocation: preach good conduct / preach a sermon / preach tolerance.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We should remember that all religions (1)_______ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_______. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_______ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_______ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_______ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ethics.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ethics" means moral principles that govern behaviour. Good conduct should rest on a foundation of ethics (morality). This links with the next line "Without the basis of morality". (नैतिकता / नीतिशास्त्र)

◦ Correct: ... the foundation of which should rest on ethics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "evil" (wickedness) and Option 3 "unconscientiousness" (lack of conscience) are the opposite of what a good foundation needs.

• Option 2 "boundaries" does not fit the moral context.

NOTE

• "Ethics" = the study of what is morally right and wrong; a set of moral principles. The passage stresses that morality/ethics is the basis of good conduct.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We should remember that all religions (1)_______ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_______. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_______ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_______ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_______ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. meaningless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause "Without the basis of morality" sets up a negative consequence, and it is joined with "and vain" (pointless). So religion would be "meaningless and vain" — without purpose. (अर्थहीन / निरर्थक)

◦ Correct: ... religion would be meaningless and vain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "useful", 2 "popular" and 3 "rational" are positive and do not fit the negative sense set up by "Without the basis of morality" and "vain".

NOTE

• "Meaningless" (without meaning/purpose) pairs naturally with "vain" (futile/pointless). The two words reinforce each other.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We should remember that all religions (1)_______ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_______. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_______ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_______ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_______ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. truthful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A truly religious person is described positively, and the blank is joined with "and unselfish". "Truthful" (honest) fits this positive pairing — "unless he is truthful and unselfish". (सत्यनिष्ठ / सच्चा)

◦ Correct: Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is truthful and unselfish.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "grotesque" (ugly/bizarre), Option 2 "lethargic" (lazy) and Option 4 "insensitive" (uncaring) are all negative and do not fit alongside "unselfish".

NOTE

• "Truthful" and "unselfish" are both virtues, so they pair naturally. Read the conjunction "and" to match the tone (here, positive).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We should remember that all religions (1)_______ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_______. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_______ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_______ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_______ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. acquire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Acquire" means to gain or obtain (something) through effort. Through constant endeavour, one could acquire (gain) absolute peace of mind. (प्राप्त करना / अर्जित करना)

◦ Correct: ... by constant endeavour ..., one could acquire absolute peace of mind.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "scatter" (to spread), Option 2 "forfeit" (to lose/give up) and Option 4 "divide" (to split) contradict the sense of gaining peace of mind.

NOTE

• Synonyms of acquire: gain, obtain, attain, get, secure.

• Antonyms: lose, forfeit, relinquish. One "acquires" knowledge, skills, wealth or, as here, peace of mind.

question: Two masses of 1 kg and 2 kg were dropped from a height of 3.2 metres. Their respective velocities just before touching the ground will be: (Assume acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s²)
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8 m/s for both.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In free fall, the final velocity depends only on the height and gravity, NOT on the mass. Using v² = u² + 2gh (with u = 0):

◦ v = √(2 × g × h) = √(2 × 10 × 3.2) = √64 = 8 m/s.

• Since the height (3.2 m) and g are the same for both, both masses hit the ground with the same velocity (8 m/s). (मुक्त पतन — वेग द्रव्यमान पर निर्भर नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• This illustrates Galileo's principle: in the absence of air resistance, all objects fall with the same acceleration (g) regardless of their mass.

• The famous "leaning tower of Pisa" experiment (attributed to Galileo) demonstrated this idea.

NOTE

• Equations of motion (uniform acceleration): v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as. In free fall, a = g (≈ 9.8 or 10 m/s²).

question: The igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are interconvertible through a continuous process called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is rock cycle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The continuous process by which the three types of rocks — igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic — are transformed from one type into another over geological time is called the "rock cycle". (शैल चक्र / रॉक साइकिल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In the rock cycle: igneous rocks (from cooled magma) → weather/erode into sediments → sedimentary rocks (by lithification) → heat/pressure → metamorphic rocks → melt into magma again, and the cycle continues.

• Lithification is the process forming sedimentary rock; metamorphism forms metamorphic rock; these are steps within the rock cycle.

NOTE

• The three rock types: Igneous (granite, basalt), Sedimentary (sandstone, limestone), Metamorphic (marble from limestone, slate from shale).

question: 'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat' is the documentary of which famous musician?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bismillah Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sange Meel Se Mulaqat" is a documentary film on the legendary shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan, directed by Goutam Ghose. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान — शहनाई वादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ustad Bismillah Khan was awarded the Bharat Ratna (2001), India's highest civilian honour. He famously played the shehnai at the Red Fort on India's first Independence Day (1947).

• The shehnai is a traditional wind instrument, often played on auspicious occasions.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs: Shehnai (Bismillah Khan), Tabla (Zakir Hussain), Flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), Violin (M. S. Gopalakrishnan), Sitar (Ravi Shankar).

question: 'The Namesake', 'Unaccustomed Earth' and 'The Lowland' are novels written by who among the following authors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jhumpa Lahiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Namesake", "Unaccustomed Earth" and "The Lowland" were all written by the Indian-American author Jhumpa Lahiri. (झुम्पा लाहिड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jhumpa Lahiri won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction (2000) for her debut short-story collection "Interpreter of Maladies".

• Her works often explore the experiences of Indian immigrants and issues of identity and belonging.

NOTE

• Author–work pairs: The God of Small Things (Arundhati Roy), The White Tiger (Aravind Adiga), Socialite Evenings (Shobha De). Jhumpa Lahiri is specifically linked with the three novels named.

question: Which of the following types of emergencies is declared under Article 360 of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Financial Emergency.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 360 of the Constitution provides for the proclamation of a "Financial Emergency" if the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen threatening the financial stability or credit of India. (अनुच्छेद 360 — वित्तीय आपातकाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The three types of emergencies:

◦ National Emergency — Article 352 (war, external aggression, armed rebellion).

◦ State Emergency / President's Rule — Article 356 (failure of constitutional machinery in a state).

◦ Financial Emergency — Article 360.

• A Financial Emergency has never been declared in India so far.

NOTE

• During a Financial Emergency, the Centre can direct states to observe financial propriety and can reduce the salaries of government servants, including judges.

question: When is the National Unity Day celebrated in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 31 October.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is celebrated on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the "Iron Man of India". (राष्ट्रीय एकता दिवस — 31 अक्टूबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It was first observed in 2014 to honour Sardar Patel's role in the unification/integration of the princely states into the Indian Union.

• The Statue of Unity in Gujarat (world's tallest statue, 182 m) is dedicated to Sardar Patel.

NOTE

• Other important days: 26 January (Republic Day), 2 October (Gandhi Jayanti / International Day of Non-Violence), 14 November (Children's Day / Nehru's birthday).

question: Which material was largely used to build the stupa at Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bricks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The stupa at Piprahwa (in Siddharthnagar district, Uttar Pradesh) was largely built using bricks. (पिपरहवा स्तूप — ईंटों से निर्मित)

• Piprahwa is believed to be associated with Kapilvastu and is famous for a relic casket said to contain the relics of the Buddha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A stupa is a mound-like Buddhist structure containing relics, used as a place of meditation and worship.

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi (built by Ashoka) is the most famous stupa in India.

NOTE

• Building materials in ancient India: burnt/baked bricks (Harappan and later stupas), sandstone (Mauryan pillars, many temples), marble (Mughal monuments).

question: How many components are there in the New India Literacy Program (NILP) scheme launched by the Union Ministry of Education in March 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The New India Literacy Programme (NILP), also called "ULLAS – Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram", has five components. (नई भारत साक्षरता कार्यक्रम — पाँच घटक)

• The five components are: (1) Foundational Literacy and Numeracy, (2) Critical Life Skills, (3) Basic Education, (4) Vocational Skills, and (5) Continuing Education.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• NILP is a centrally sponsored scheme (2022–2027) aimed at making non-literate adults (aged 15 and above) literate.

• It is aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

NOTE

• "ULLAS" stands for Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society. The scheme uses volunteers and digital/mobile technology for adult education.

question: In June 2023, which country conferred the 'Order of the Nile' award on Narendra Modi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Egypt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2023, Egypt conferred its highest state honour, the "Order of the Nile", on Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his state visit. (ऑर्डर ऑफ द नाइल — मिस्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The "Order of the Nile" (Kiladat al Nil) is the highest state honour of Egypt, awarded to heads of state and those who have rendered exceptional service to the nation.

• PM Modi has received the highest civilian honours of several countries, reflecting India's growing diplomatic ties.

NOTE

• Some other honours received by PM Modi: Order of Zayed (UAE), Order of St. Andrew (Russia), Legion of Merit (USA), Order of the Companion of the Q (various), and honours from Bhutan, Maldives, etc.

question: Who among the following adopted the policy of consolidation in place of expansion by eliminating the rebels?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghiyasuddin Balban.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ghiyasuddin Balban (r. 1266–1287) of the Slave/Mamluk dynasty adopted a policy of consolidation rather than expansion. He focused on crushing internal rebellions, suppressing the nobility (the "Chihalgani/Chalisa" group of forty) and restoring the prestige and authority of the Sultanate. (बलबन — विस्तार के स्थान पर सुदृढ़ीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Balban followed a policy of "Blood and Iron" to deal with rebels and threats.

• He propounded the theory of the divine right of kings ("Zill-i-Ilahi" — Shadow of God) and introduced the court customs of Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the feet).

NOTE

• Balban created a strong, centralised administration and a powerful army/spy system to face Mongol invasions and internal revolts.

question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what was the proportion of population in multidimensional poverty (Headcount Ratio) in urban India in 2019-2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.27%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023: A Progress Review by NITI Aayog, the proportion of the population that was multidimensionally poor in urban India (2019-21) was about 5.27%. (शहरी भारत में बहुआयामी गरीबी — 5.27%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Multidimensional poverty was much higher in rural India than in urban India.

• The MPI measures poverty across three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — through 12 indicators, based on the global OPHI–UNDP methodology.

NOTE

• A person is "multidimensionally poor" if deprived in at least one-third (weighted) of the indicators. The report noted a significant fall in poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21.

question: In which of the followings years was the National Population Policy of India released?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Population Policy (NPP) of India was released in the year 2000. Its immediate objective was to address the unmet needs for contraception, health infrastructure and health personnel. (राष्ट्रीय जनसंख्या नीति — 2000)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The NPP 2000's medium-term goal was to bring the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) to replacement level (2.1) by 2010, and the long-term goal was to achieve a stable population by 2045.

• India launched its first official family planning programme in 1952 (the first country in the world to do so).

NOTE

• India's population dynamics are studied through the Census and the Sample Registration System (SRS). India became the world's most populous country around 2023.

question:
Match the political parties of British India in column A with their respective founders in column B.

Column A: a. All India Forward Bloc  b. Arya Samaj  c. The Congress Socialist Party  d. The Indian National Liberal Federation   |   Column B: i. Dayananda Sarasvati  ii. Jai Prakash Narayan  iii. Surendra Nath Banerjee  iv. Subhash Chandra Bose
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of parties/organisations with their founders is:

◦ a. All India Forward Bloc → iv. Subhash Chandra Bose (founded 1939).

◦ b. Arya Samaj → i. Dayananda Saraswati (founded 1875).

◦ c. The Congress Socialist Party → ii. Jai Prakash Narayan (founded 1934, with Acharya Narendra Deva).

◦ d. The Indian National Liberal Federation → iii. Surendra Nath Banerjee (founded 1919).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1 (a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii).

Additional Information

• Subhas Chandra Bose left the Congress and founded the Forward Bloc; he later led the Azad Hind Fauj (INA).

• Surendra Nath Banerjee was a moderate leader, called the "Indian Burke" / "Rashtraguru".

NOTE

• The Congress Socialist Party (CSP) was a socialist group within the Congress. Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) later led the "Total Revolution" movement in the 1970s.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Union Government budget in India?

a. The Budget reflects the vision of the government in fulfilling the aspirations of people.  b. The Budget is the summary report of the financial performance of the government in power.  c. The Budget provides details of expenditures meted out by various Union Government ministries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is All a, b and c.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three statements about the Union Budget are correct:

◦ a. The Budget reflects the government's vision and priorities in meeting people's aspirations.

◦ b. It is a summary/report of the financial performance and plans of the government.

◦ c. It provides detailed estimates of the expenditure of various ministries and departments.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Union Budget (Annual Financial Statement) is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution.

• It has two parts: the Revenue Budget (revenue receipts and expenditure) and the Capital Budget (capital receipts and expenditure).

NOTE

• The Budget is usually presented on 1 February. The Finance Minister presents it in the Lok Sabha; it must be passed by Parliament before the start of the financial year (1 April).

question: A ______ happens in chess when a player gives up material during the initiation to seek some kind of compensation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gambit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In chess, a "gambit" is an opening in which a player sacrifices some material (usually a pawn) in the early stage of the game to gain a positional or developmental advantage/compensation. (गैम्बिट — मोहरे का बलिदान)

◦ Example: The "Queen's Gambit" is a famous chess opening.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Castling" is a special move involving the king and a rook, used for the king's safety.

• "Blockade" is a strategy of blocking an opponent's pawn/piece.

• The word "gambit" is also used generally to mean a calculated move or ploy to gain an advantage.

NOTE

• Chess terms: checkmate, stalemate, castling, gambit, en passant, fork, pin, zugzwang. India's Viswanathan Anand was a five-time World Chess Champion; D. Gukesh became the youngest World Champion in 2024.

question: Kaal Baisakhi belongs to which state from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kaal Baisakhi" (also called Nor'westers) refers to the violent thunderstorms with strong winds and rain that occur in the pre-monsoon season (April–May) mainly over West Bengal (and Assam, Odisha). (काल बैसाखी — पश्चिम बंगाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• These storms are locally known as "Kalbaisakhi" in West Bengal and "Bordoichila" in Assam.

• Though destructive, they bring some relief from the summer heat and are helpful for crops like jute, rice and tea.

NOTE

• Local pre-monsoon storms/winds: Kaal Baisakhi (West Bengal/Assam), Loo (hot dry winds of North India), Mango showers (Karnataka/Kerala — help mango ripening), Cherry blossoms (coffee in Karnataka).

question:
Which of the following statements is NOT true about Plastids?

A) Starch, oils and protein granules are stored in chromoplasts.  B) They have their own ribosomes.  C) They have their own DNA.  D) Stroma is found in chloroplast.
option_1: Starch, oils and protein granules are stored in chromoplasts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Starch, oils and protein granules are stored in chromoplasts (this statement is NOT true).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement A is incorrect: starch, oils and protein granules are stored in "leucoplasts" (colourless plastids), NOT in chromoplasts. Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments (giving colour to flowers and fruits). (ल्यूकोप्लास्ट — भंडारण; क्रोमोप्लास्ट — रंगीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other statements are true: plastids have their own DNA and ribosomes (they are semi-autonomous organelles), and the stroma (a fluid matrix) is found in chloroplasts.

• Types of plastids: Chloroplasts (green, photosynthesis), Chromoplasts (coloured pigments), Leucoplasts (colourless, storage).

NOTE

• Leucoplasts are further of three types: Amyloplasts (store starch), Elaioplasts (store oils/fats) and Aleuroplasts/Proteinoplasts (store proteins).

question: In the animal kingdom, which of the following phyla includes animals with a segmented body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annelida.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phylum "Annelida" includes animals with a segmented (metamerically divided) body — the body is divided into a series of ring-like segments. (एनिलिडा — खंडयुक्त शरीर)

◦ Examples: earthworm, leech, Nereis.

• The name comes from the Latin "annulus", meaning "little ring".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Arthropoda also shows segmentation but is distinguished by jointed legs and an exoskeleton (e.g., insects, spiders, crabs); however, "segmented body" is the defining feature emphasised for Annelida.

• Mollusca (snails, octopus) have soft, unsegmented bodies; Chordata have a notochord.

NOTE

• Annelids have a true coelom (coelomate) and a closed circulatory system. The earthworm is called the "farmer's friend" for improving soil fertility.

question: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Iron Age in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mehrauli iron pillar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mehrauli iron pillar" (in Delhi) is NOT associated with the Iron Age — it belongs to the Gupta period (around the 4th–5th century CE) and is famous for its rust-resistant iron, showing the advanced metallurgy of that later era. (महरौली लौह स्तंभ — गुप्त काल, लौह युग नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Associated with the Iron Age in India: iron smelting, the Painted Grey Ware (PGW) culture and (in the later phase) the Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) culture.

• The Iron Age in India roughly corresponds to the later Vedic period and the use of iron tools/weapons.

NOTE

• The Mehrauli Iron Pillar stands near the Qutub Minar and bears a Sanskrit inscription; it has famously not rusted for over 1,500 years.

question: Which of the following committees was set up to investigate into the infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hunter Committee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Hunter Committee" (formally the Disorders Inquiry Committee), headed by Lord William Hunter, was set up in 1919 to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar). (हंटर समिति — जलियांवाला बाग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre was ordered by General Reginald Dyer, who fired on a peaceful gathering, killing hundreds.

• In protest, Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood and Mahatma Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal.

NOTE

• Other committees for SSC: Sadler Commission (university education, 1917), Butler Committee (relations between princely states and the Crown, 1927), Simon Commission (constitutional reforms, 1927).

question: From which of the following countries has the Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of the Concurrent List?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The concept of the "Concurrent List" (a list of subjects on which both the Centre and the States can legislate) was borrowed by the Indian Constitution from Australia. (समवर्ती सूची — ऑस्ट्रेलिया से)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• From Australia, India also borrowed the ideas of freedom of trade and commerce, and the joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.

• The three lists in the Seventh Schedule are: Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

NOTE

• Borrowed features: Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review, Impeachment (USA); Parliamentary system, Rule of Law (UK); Directive Principles (Ireland); Emergency provisions (Germany/USSR); Concurrent List, Trade & Commerce (Australia).

question: __________ was launched by the Government of India in 2020 to make the country and its citizens independent and self-sufficient in all respects.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan" (Self-Reliant India Campaign) was launched by the Government of India in May 2020 to make the country and its citizens independent and self-sufficient in all respects, especially in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. (आत्मनिर्भर भारत अभियान — 2020)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The campaign was built on five pillars: Economy, Infrastructure, System, Vibrant Demography and Demand.

• It included a large economic stimulus package and promoted "Vocal for Local" and Make in India.

NOTE

• Related schemes: Make in India (2014), Startup India, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, One District One Product (ODOP) — all aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing and self-reliance.

question: Which of the following war dances is performed in Ngada festival and is a performed by the tribes of Nagaland?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rengma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rengma" is a war dance performed during the Ngada festival by the tribes of Nagaland (the Rengma Nagas). It reflects the martial traditions and cultural heritage of the Naga tribes. (रेंगमा — नागालैंड का युद्ध नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nagaland is famous for its vibrant tribal culture and the grand Hornbill Festival (December).

• "Jawara" is a folk dance of Madhya Pradesh; "Dalkhai" is from Odisha; "Garadi" is from Puducherry.

NOTE

• War dances are common among many Indian tribes, celebrating valour and community. Nagaland has 16+ major tribes, each with distinct dances and festivals.

question: Which edition of the Pro Kabaddi League was started in December 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 10th edition (Season 10) of the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) started in December 2023. (प्रो कबड्डी लीग — 10वाँ संस्करण)

• Season 10 was won by the Puneri Paltan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Pro Kabaddi League is a professional franchise-based kabaddi league in India, launched in 2014, which greatly boosted the popularity of the sport.

• Kabaddi is a traditional Indian contact team sport; India has dominated the Kabaddi World Cup and Asian Games.

NOTE

• Court dimensions: men's kabaddi 13 m × 10 m. A "raider" enters the opponents' half and tries to tag defenders while chanting "kabaddi".

question: Mallika Sarabhai was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 2010 for her contribution to which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mallika Sarabhai was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 2010 for her contribution to the field of Dance (Art). She is an acclaimed exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi. (मल्लिका साराभाई — नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mallika Sarabhai is the daughter of the famous scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai (father of the Indian space programme) and the renowned classical dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai.

• She is also a social activist and runs the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad.

NOTE

• The Padma Awards (Bharat Ratna is separate) — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri — are given in fields such as Art, Social Work, Public Affairs, Science, Sports, Medicine and Literature.
